newsitem.title: USA: US merger layoffs fall 84 pct May-Aug - Challenger.
newsitem.headline: US merger layoffs fall 84 pct May-Aug - Challenger.

text.p: U.S. layoffs resulting from mergers declined 84 percent in May through August 1996 compared with the same four months of 1995, according to a report by international outplacement firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas Inc.
A total of 6,083 jobs were cut due to mergers in the second four months of 1996, down from 37,381 in the same period last year, the report said.
The May-through-August 1996 total was 71 percent lower than January-through-April, it said.

"The sharp merger-related layoff decrease began as the presidential primaries were ending, which may lead to conjecture that some of the larger merged companies may be postponing layoffs until after the election," executive vice president John A. Challenger said in a statement.
Companies may be putting off job cuts to avoid becoming a campaign issue, he said.

More than 5,300 U.S. companies have merged so far in 1996, up from about 4,300 in the same period last year, the report said. Positions cut after the mergers have tended to be those of executives and managers rather than laborers, it said.
"Skilled labor has become a protected class as many newly merged firms have found it makes better economic sense to (cut) higher-salaried employees," Challenger said.
